A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LVFace, with matching backbone concepts and headline benchmark results. All supplied pages, equations, figures and tables support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix, although v1 has a dangling reference to Appendix A.

before.justification: V1 reports original LVFace verification results on MFR-Ongoing and IJB-C in Table 1.

after.justification: V2 retains original LVFace results and adds benchmark comparisons, ablations and feature visualizations in Tables 2-5 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: V1 combines prototype stabilization and removal of negative sampling in its second training stage. V2 separates these into distinct stages, replaces the later-stage objective with classifier-plus-prototype losses, and introduces cosine-threshold stage transitions through CSS. These substantially revise the training procedure while largely retaining the ViT backbone.

E1.justification: V2 adds LVFace training on Glint360K alongside WebFace42M and evaluation on IJB-B, expanding the training population and evaluation coverage. V1's proposed model is evaluated only after WebFace42M training on MFR-Ongoing and IJB-C; Glint360K appears there only as a comparator's training dataset.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds ArcFace and AdaFace comparisons at R50/R100/R200 scales, plain ViT baselines, and smaller TransFace variants. ViT-P12S8 is removed. V1's TransFace-L comparison is retained in Table 2, while UniFace, UniTSFace, TopoFR and Partial FC remain in Table 1.

E3.justification: The stated training budget changes from 40+60 epochs to 60+60 epochs, and the reported base loss/margin changes from ArcFace with 0.5 to CosFace with 0.4. V2 also introduces multiple model sizes, controlled loss/stage comparisons and IJB-C evaluation at FAR=1e-6. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V1 contains no reported ablation studies. V2 adds model/data scaling, ArcFace-versus-CosFace dependency, and cumulative training-stage ablations in Tables 3-5. Figure 3 additionally examines feature distributions for eight identities across initialization and the three training stages.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's phrase 'statistically significant improvements' is not accompanied by a statistical testing procedure or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All headline LVFace values in Table 1 remain unchanged, including MR-All 98.49 and IJB-C 97.25/98.06. V2 adds Partial FC's previously missing IJB-C FAR=1e-4 result of 98.00 and extensive Glint360K, IJB-B and ablation results. For example, Table 5 reports MR-All 97.27 for plain ViT-L and 98.49 for full PCO; this is a newly reported comparison, not a cross-version performance gain.

T1.justification: The central mathematical loss definitions change from v1 Equations 17-19 to the classifier/prototype similarity objectives in v2 Equations 8, 11 and 12. V2 also formalizes the open-set problem and introduces the mean squared cosine statistic and threshold rule for CSS in Equation 13. Neither version provides formal convergence proofs.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes exploring orthogonal combinations of existing face losses for largely unchanged ViTs. V2 makes three-stage PCO and CSS explicit central contributions and adds claims about multi-stage superiority, scalability and feature compatibility with VLMs/LLMs. The broad state-of-the-art and challenge-ranking claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of hard-positive centroid instability and progressive boundary refinement, interprets the Glint360K Base-to-Large plateau as a data-capacity constraint, and discusses computational overhead. It also explicitly acknowledges TopoFR's better Mask result, which v1 does not discuss. These substantially expand mechanisms, applicability qualifications and result interpretation.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's sparse optimizer and hardware description, v2 specifies RetinaFace preprocessing, 112x112 crops, augmentation, embedding-head layers, learning rate, AdamW coefficients, polynomial decay, batch sizes and mixed precision. It also supplies pseudocode, a negative-sampling ratio of 0.1 and CSS thresholds of 0.2/0.35. Many are newly disclosed details rather than established changes to earlier implementation.

R1.justification: V2 substantially refocuses related work toward metric learning, adaptive margins, inter-class regularization and ViT optimization. It adds works including FaceNet, UniformFace, RegularFace and part-based ViTs while removing much of v1's general vision-transformer survey. Contribution positioning shifts from exploring existing losses to a specific progressive optimization and scheduling framework.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodology are extensively rewritten. V2 moves architecture and margin-loss background into a new Preliminary section, organizes the method around named stages and CSS, and restructures experiments into benchmark, ablation and efficiency subsections. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a two-column layout, replaces the original overview/backbone figures with new PCO illustrations, and adds a four-panel feature visualization. It reformats Table 1, introduces four additional tables and adds Algorithm 1. This substantially changes both visual explanation and document presentation.

improvement.justification: V1 offers one headline comparison with little evidence isolating its training choices. V2 addresses that deficiency through loss, stage and scaling ablations, broader comparisons, and substantially fuller equations, pseudocode and implementation details. Some new claims exceed the evidence, including VLM/LLM compatibility and across-scale superiority despite exceptions in Table 2. Nevertheless, the controlled analyses and clearer specification substantially improve the paper's scientific support and reproducibility; the unchanged headline scores are not the basis for this judgment.
